name: Bubonic plague (flea- and louse-borne, as in the Second Pandemic)

reproduction_number_range.source: Dean et al. 2018, PNAS, doi 10.1073/pnas.1715640115, full text at pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5819418 (opened): the human-ectoparasite model gives an estimated R0 from 1.48 (Eyam) to 1.91 (Barcelona) across nine pre-industrial outbreaks (Table 3 and Results); the pneumonic and rat-flea model variants give other ranges and are not used here

transmissibility_per_day.source: The midpoint of the sourced reproduction number range (1.695) divided by the infectious days, rounded

case_fatality.source: WHO plague fact sheet, who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/plague: 'a case-fatality ratio of 30% to 60% for the bubonic type'; 0.45 is the midpoint (the page gives no untreated qualifier for that range)

immunity.source: No source found: the WHO plague fact sheet makes no statement on immunity, and Dean et al. 2018 (PMC5819418) say their models ignore immunity; lifelong immunity is a labelled assumption

stage.incubating.source: WHO plague fact sheet: 'an incubation period of one to seven days'; the 4 day mean is the midpoint. Shape 4 is a middling spread, not sourced

stage.infectious.source: Dean et al. 2018 (PMC5819418, Table 2): an average duration of infection of 10 days for bubonic plague in humans in the rat-flea model (the human-ectoparasite model splits it into 8 mildly and 2 highly infectious days, the same 10 total). Shape 2 is a broad spread, not sourced

density_exponent.source: Heuristic inside the range Rader et al. 2020 supports (crowded cities see longer epidemics with larger attack rates; weaker than linear); vary across the ensemble
